question:
A curve passes through the origin, and at every point $(x,y)$ on it the slope of the tangent is equal to the sum of the coordinates of that point. Thus, the geometric condition gives $\frac{dy}{dx}=x+y$. To determine the equation of the curve, students must first rearrange this relation into the standard form of a first-order linear differential equation. They then use an integrating factor to obtain the general family and finally use the fact that the required curve passes through $(0,0)$ to select the appropriate member. The task connects the tangent-slope description of a curve with the solution of a linear differential equation.

(a) Form the differential equation from the given slope condition and rewrite it in standard linear form.

(b) Determine the integrating factor of the linear differential equation.

(c) Solve the equation to obtain its general solution.

(d) Use the fact that the curve passes through the origin to obtain the required equation of the curve.
explanation:
(a)
The slope of the tangent is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=x+y$$

Rearranging, $$\frac{dy}{dx}-y=x$$

This is of the standard form $\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q$, where $$P=-1,\qquad Q=x$$

(b)
The integrating factor is $$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int P\,dx}=e^{\int-1\,dx}=e^{-x}$$

(c)
Multiplying the equation by $e^{-x}$, $$e^{-x}\frac{dy}{dx}-e^{-x}y=xe^{-x}$$

Therefore, $$\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{-x})=xe^{-x}$$

Integrating, $$ye^{-x}=\int xe^{-x}\,dx+C$$

Using integration by parts, $$\int xe^{-x}\,dx=-(x+1)e^{-x}$$

Hence, $$ye^{-x}=-(x+1)e^{-x}+C$$

Multiplying by $e^x$, $$y=-x-1+Ce^x$$

(d)
The curve passes through $(0,0)$. Therefore, substituting $x=0$ and $y=0$, $$0=-0-1+C$$

Thus, $C=1$.

Hence the required equation of the curve is $$y=e^x-x-1$$

This curve satisfies both the given tangent-slope condition and the condition of passing through the origin.

options.B:
(a) $\frac{dy}{dx}-y=x$, so $P=-1$
(b) I.F. $=e^{-x}$
(c) $y=-x-1+Ce^x$
(d) Through the origin, $C=1$ and $y=e^x-x-1$
